thread:
kevin: quick heads-up — ran a focused perf sweep on the new coalescer behavior with prefix/prompt caching turned on for a production-like traffic replay. saw an odd latency bump when prefix-hit ratio > ~65%.

maria: can you paste the profiling output? was this p50 or p95 impact?

kevin: p50 went up ~10-12% during the steady phase, p95 stayed within SLO but tail widened a bit. overall throughput unchanged. root cause looks like extra micro-batching due to opportunistic padding interacting badly with kernel selection fallback.

sam: do you mean the runtime started picking the generic fused-attn kernel for many short residual sequences? i've seen that before when the estimated workspace changed.

kevin: exactly. when prefix-cache hits are high we end up with more short inference tails and the kernel selector thinks the int8/quant kernels are suboptimal because the token-length distribution shifts. it then picks the fallback that has lower setup overhead but worse per-token cost for our common path. profiling snippet below (condensed):

```
# condensed perf counters
workload: replay-2026-03-10
prefix_hit_rate: 72%
seq_len_mean: 28
seq_len_median: 12
kernel_choice_breakdown: generic_fused: 48% | int8_fused: 30% | cuda_opt: 22%
p50_latency_ms: baseline 18 -> experiment 20
p95_latency_ms: baseline 48 -> experiment 50
kv_cache_lookup_ms: ~0.4 per call
packing_overhead_ms: +1.6 (opportunistic pad path)
```

maria: interesting. so cache hits are making more short requests available to the coalescer but our batching heuristic is still tuned for longer tails. Maybe we need a separate small-seq policy that biases kernel selection and packing decisions.

sam: agreed. proposal: introduce a "micro-batch" path when predicted post-cache tokens <= 16. that path should force the low-latency kernel (even if less throughput optimal) and reduce opportunistic padding to a minimal floor. also add an explicit token_budget_target per queue class.

kevin: i sketched a config patch we could try in canary:

```
continuous_batching:
  token_budget_targets:
    small_seq: 24
    default: 64
  opportunistic_padding:
    enabled: true
    max_extra_tokens: 8
    floor: 1
  kernel_selector:
    bias_for_latency_when_predicted_tokens_le: 16
  queue_policies:
    micro_batch_shelf_ms: 5
    default_shelf_ms: 12
```

maria: +1 to micro-batch shelf and explicit token budgets. also add a heuristic: if prefix_hit_rate > 60% and avg_seq_len < 30, reduce the candidate batch max by 25% (so we avoid accidental coalescing of many tiny tails).

sam: i'd also add a small randomized jitter to the shelf timer to avoid synchronous wakes from many clients. 2-3ms jitter should be enough.

kevin: good catch. i'll add jitter. ops-bot — can we run a 1h canary replay against prod-capacity with these settings, compare p50/p95 and kernel distribution? tag the run with "coalescer-pcache-microbatch-2026"

ops-bot: scheduled canary run: coalescer-pcache-microbatch-2026 on 1742012000 (2h window). replay dataset: replay-2026-03-10. will upload perf traces to /tmp/perf/coalescer-pcache-microbatch-2026.trace

maria: if the canary looks good let's gate it behind a small rollout (10% nodes) and add an automatic revert if p50 regresses >5% or p95 regresses >10% for 5 consecutive minutes. also add an isolated kernel selector flag so we can toggle the bias without touching other batching knobs.

kevin: copying plan into PR description and will attach profiling artifacts. PR will be small: add token budget class, shelf jitter, micro-batch kernel bias, and the prefix-hit rate short-circuit.

sam: one more note — we should instrument the KV cache stats per-batch (hit count, avg prefix length) so we can correlate batch composition to kernel choices. that will help avoid blind tuning.

kevin: agreed. i'll add telemetry fields: batch.kv_hit_ratio, batch.avg_prefix_tokens, batch.predicted_postcache_tokens.

maria: sounds actionable. thanks kevin. if canary passes i'll take the rollout. :+1:

kevin: thanks all — i'll post results once ops-bot uploads the traces.
